## Design

### 2026-11-05: I started off my project by doing some research on what I planned to do. I originally planned to make some sort of clock that sprayed water but that proved difficult given the time constraints. I then

**5h**

I started off my project by doing some research on what I planned to do. I originally planned to make some sort of clock that sprayed water but that proved difficult given the time constraints. I then shifted towards the macropod project. It seemed fun to design an extension of your keyboard that has its own key binds you can use. At last, I settled with the XIAO RP2040 with 4 buttons and 7 pins on each side and began mapping things out. I began my project on KiCad where I created a folder and started the schematic. I first inserted two JConn 01x07s and 4 SW_Push. I labeled and closed off the connectors to get this schematic. There weren't any major challenges yet except researching. Everything else was remotely easy. There was, however, a problem that came up in the ERC (electric rules checker) regarding the GND power input and the unconnected "no connect flag." That was fixed pretty quickly.

### 2026-11-05: This time, I started off by adding the footprints. I had to decide on what type of keys I wanted to use and the footprints for each of these parts which were somewhat challenging.  Probably the hardes

**6h**

This time, I started off by adding the footprints. I had to decide on what type of keys I wanted to use and the footprints for each of these parts which were somewhat challenging.  Probably the hardest part. I then updated the schematic into the PCB editor, and it looked kind of simple so I decided to add one of those rotation buttons called a rotary encoder. I chose a specific type and went back to the schematic to update it. I then imported it into the PCB editor and began to work the dimensions. I arranged the buttons into a 2x2 shape and set the distance between J1 and J2 to be 15.24mm apart with the USB facing up to fit the part. I then added the Edge.Cuts border around in a 71x46mm dimension. There were some minor challenges along the way, and I had to get some help with choosing the specific parts. Dimensioning was also kind of annoying. After this, I'll be adding mounting holes to put it in a 3D designed case.

### 2026-11-08: I started by creating the mounting holes for the macropad. I went back to the schematic and inserted 3 of these holes so I could screw them into a case. I then assigned a footprint for each and saved

**10h**

I started by creating the mounting holes for the macropad. I went back to the schematic and inserted 3 of these holes so I could screw them into a case. I then assigned a footprint for each and saved it into the PCB. After, I updated the PCB editor I put the mounting holes in the top left, bottom left, and bottom right of the PCB. Once I had the mounting holes, I started working on the case. I started the document on Onshape where I first created a sketch on the top plane. I then drew a 76x51 square for the outer casing and a 72x47 square for the inner wall making the wall 4mm thick. I then extruded cylinders for the PCB and the screws. Afterwards, I assembled everything together, and imported the PCB from KiCad. Once everything was assembled, I prepared for the next day. All in all, the hardest part was the wiring. I had to make sure the wire wasn't too close to the copper padding. I also had to alternate between the front and back wiring.
